name: Permissions
summary: Decide which actions Claude Code may take on its own, which need your OK, and which are never allowed.
what: Before Claude edits a file, runs a command or uses a tool, Claude Code checks your permission rules. Each rule names a tool, optionally narrowed down, such as Bash(npm run test *) or Read(./.env), and sits in one of three lists: allow, ask or deny. A permission mode sets the overall behaviour, from asking about everything to accepting file edits automatically.

impact.title: Fewer interruptions
impact.detail: Allow the commands you run all the time, such as tests and linters, and Claude stops asking about them.

impact.title: Hard limits
impact.detail: A deny rule always wins, so secrets files or risky commands stay off limits whatever else is allowed.

impact.title: The right pace for the task
impact.detail: Switch modes with Shift+Tab: review each edit, accept edits automatically, or only plan.

howItWorks: When Claude asks, choosing "don't ask again" saves an allow rule for that project.
Use /permissions to see, add and remove rules, or edit the permissions block of a settings file.
Rules are checked in the order deny, then ask, then allow; the first match decides.
Pick a starting mode with --permission-mode or the defaultMode setting, and cycle modes in a session with Shift+Tab.
Bash rules match command text, so they are a convenience, not a security boundary; use deny rules and the sandbox for protection.

events.note: Already part of Claude Code when the changelog began with this version.
Ask rules: always confirm before chosen tools run.
